did_you_know.text: Did you know? Jehoshaphat strengthened his position in the kingdom after ascending the throne, and the text notes that he also grew stronger against the kingdom of Israel.
Did you know? Jehoshaphat stationed troops and officials in the fortified cities of Judah, as well as in the cities of Ephraim that his father Asa had captured.
Did you know? Jehoshaphat’s faithfulness is shown by the fact that he followed the ways of David, did not seek the Baals, and sought the God of his father.
Did you know? Along with strengthening his rule, Jehoshaphat removed the high places and Asherah poles from Judah, thus continuing the reforms in the worship of the Lord throughout the kingdom.
Did you know? In the third year of his reign, Jehoshaphat sent officials to the cities of Judah to teach the people.
Did you know? The teaching delegation included officials, Levites, and priests. They traveled throughout the cities of Judah with the Book of the Law of the Lord and taught the people.
Did you know? According to the text, the fear of the Lord fell on the kingdoms surrounding Judah, so they did not wage war against Jehoshaphat.
Did you know? The Philistines brought Jehoshaphat tribute and silver, and the Arabs brought him 7,700 rams and 7,700 male goats.
Did you know? Jehoshaphat continued to grow stronger. He built fortresses, or strongholds, in Judah, as well as store cities for supplies and treasures.

Did you know? At the end of the chapter, the commanders of thousands and the mighty warriors of Judah and Benjamin are listed, and the text emphasizes that they served the king in addition to the soldiers stationed in the fortified cities.
